numberAndPlaceValue: Count from 0 in multiples of 4, 8, 50 and 100
Recognise place value in three-digit numbers; compare and order numbers to 1,000
Find 10 or 100 more or less; read and write Roman numerals to 12
additionSubtraction: Add and subtract numbers mentally, including three-digit and ones/tens/hundreds
Add and subtract three-digit numbers using formal written methods where appropriate
Estimate and use inverse operations to check
multiplicationDivision: Recall and use 3, 4 and 8 multiplication tables and related division facts
Write and calculate multiplication and division statements, including two-digit by one-digit multiplication
Solve problems involving scaling and correspondence
fractions: Count in tenths; understand tenths as fractions and decimals
Recognise, find and write unit and non-unit fractions of amounts
Compare and order fractions with the same denominator; add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
measurement: Measure, compare, add and subtract length, mass, volume/capacity
Tell and write time to nearest minute; use 12/24-hour clocks and Roman numerals
Recognise pounds and pence and solve money problems
geometry: Recognise angles as a property of shape and identify right angles
Identify horizontal, vertical, perpendicular and parallel lines
statistics: Interpret and present data using bar charts, pictograms and tables
Solve one-step and two-step questions about data
reasoning: Solve problems using number facts and appropriate operations
Explain and check methods using inverse operations and estimation

numberAndPlaceValue: Recognise place value in four-digit numbers; order and compare to 10,000
Round to nearest 10, 100 or 1,000; read Roman numerals to 100
additionSubtraction: Add and subtract numbers with up to four digits using formal written methods
Estimate and use inverse operations to check answers
Solve two-step addition and subtraction problems
multiplicationDivision: Recall multiplication and division facts for all tables up to 12 × 12
Use place value, known facts and written methods for two-digit and three-digit numbers multiplied by one digit
Divide up to three-digit numbers by one digit, including remainders in context
fractions: Recognise and show families of equivalent fractions
Count in hundredths; recognise hundredths as fractions and decimals
Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator; solve fractions of quantities
measurement: Convert between common units of length, mass, volume and time
Measure and calculate perimeter of rectilinear shapes
Read, write and convert time between analogue and digital 12/24-hour clocks
geometry: Compare and classify shapes, including quadrilaterals and triangles
Identify acute and obtuse angles and compare angles
Identify lines of symmetry in 2D shapes; complete symmetric figures
Describe positions on a 2D grid and plot specified points
statistics: Interpret and present discrete and continuous data using appropriate graphical methods, including line graphs
Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using information in charts and graphs
reasoning: Solve multi-step problems and explain efficient methods
Use mathematical reasoning to investigate patterns and justify conclusions

progressionNotes: Year 3 builds secure three-digit number understanding; Year 4 extends this to four-digit numbers and rounding to 1,000.
Year 3 prioritises 3, 4 and 8 times tables; Year 4 consolidates all multiplication tables to 12 × 12.
Fractions progress from tenths in Year 3 to hundredths and equivalent fractions in Year 4.
Measurement develops from perimeter of simple shapes in Year 3 to perimeter and area in Year 4.
Statistics develops from pictograms, bar charts and tables to line graphs and broader data interpretation.
status: draft progression map requiring educator and statutory-source verification
